doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Selling CDs and tips with the old man in the train station
summary: She explains how she passed the tip bucket and sold CDs mid-solo, earning about 800 a week, and says that is why the Foundation hired her.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: No, I could never afford all those harps. I could afford one, in the key that he was in, and there was only like one or two songs that I could do because of it. But really his purpose in inviting me to play with him – because at first I was just terrible – his purpose was to have a little blonde in a dress going to pass the tip bucket, and then when I became like an asset and I recorded us, and I was his CD partner and I was selling the CDs for 12 bucks apiece, we started rolling in the dough and that’s when, you know, my playing got much better. I would take this wailing solo. We would have like 50 people in the train station, this was just before 9/11 when people still gathered. And I would go sell the CDs while the song was still going on, I’d take my solo, and while we were in that moment I’d start selling the CDs and passing the tip bucket before the crowd dispersed. So I knew how to raise money, okay? That’s why the Jazz Foundation hired me.
I was going to say, did you put that on your resume? “Played blues in the subway.”

No, they knew my – that’s too funny – no I had a very successful – I had my 15 minutes of fame with another charity for the homeless selling the “Street News,” the newspapers that allowed the homeless to work and buy their own food, and that was successful and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
